reference_memory.normal_pattern: The normal pattern is a piecewise-constant, step-like signal with a robust period of ~98 points (1 cycle per 98 points), as confirmed by the reference_cycle_plan and estimated_period. Each cycle consists of three phases: a rapid upward step (~1–2 points), a sustained plateau (≈30–40 points), and a rapid downward step (~1–2 points), forming a trapezoidal pulse. Plateau levels vary across cycles but remain stable within each cycle; baseline shifts gradually across long windows (e.g., candidate 2 shows a slow downward drift over 5 cycles). Amplitude (peak-to-trough) ranges 1.0–2.7 in robust-standardized units, with 90th-percentile amplitude ~2.0–2.7. Peaks are flat-topped with sharp vertical transitions; troughs are similarly flat and well-defined. Noise is negligible—roughness and curvature are zero in catalog, and visual inspection shows no jitter or high-frequency variation. Boundary truncation is minimal; all candidates begin/end mid-cycle but preserve full motif structure. Acceptable variation includes: (1) monotonic baseline drift (slope_per_point ≈ ±0.003), (2) plateau height shifting between cycles (e.g., from −1.0 to +1.0), (3) occasional single-cycle amplitude spikes (e.g., candidate 2 at index 1847), which appear isolated and do not disrupt periodicity. The core invariant is the 98-point cadence and trapezoidal step morphology.

reference_profiles.description: Single-cycle (98-point) excerpt showing one complete trapezoidal pulse: starts near −1.25, steps up sharply to −0.25 around point 10, plateaus until ~point 35, drops sharply to −0.75 at ~point 40, plateaus again, then drops to −1.25 near point 80 and stays flat. Very clean, no drift, minimal amplitude (≈1.0). Visually the most ‘textbook’ cycle.

Three-cycle (294-point) excerpt with clear periodic repetition of trapezoidal pulses. Plateau levels shift upward across cycles (from −1.0 → 0.0 → +1.0), and a mild positive trend (slope ≈ +0.003) is visible. One pulse (around index 1016) has a slightly taller peak (+1.2 vs typical +1.0), but morphology remains intact. No noise or distortion.

Three-cycle excerpt with stronger baseline drift (downward slope ≈ +0.001, but median rises from 0.3 to 0.7 due to offset), and one prominent spike at index 1847 (peak ≈ 2.0, double typical amplitude). Despite this, all other cycles match the trapezoidal motif precisely. The spike is isolated and does not affect adjacent cycles—likely a transient anomaly, but the underlying pattern remains highly consistent.

Five-cycle (490-point) excerpt showing robust periodicity over extended duration. Plateau levels alternate between low (−1.0) and mid (0.0–1.0) states; one cycle (around 2776) exhibits a tall spike (~1.7), similar to candidate 2 but less extreme. Trend is mildly positive. All transitions remain sharp and flat-topped. Best for assessing long-term stability and cycle-to-cycle consistency.

reference_memory.selection_guidance: Prefer reference 0 for queries matching a single clean cycle (e.g., short query windows or isolated anomalies). Use reference 1 for queries with mild upward drift and 3-cycle context. Reference 3 is optimal for long queries (>300 points) or when assessing multi-cycle consistency; its 5-cycle span provides strongest evidence of periodic stability. Reference 2 should be used cautiously—only when a query contains a similar isolated high spike *and* otherwise matches the trapezoidal motif; otherwise, treat its spike as contamination and downweight.
uncertainties: Whether isolated high-amplitude spikes (e.g., candidate 2’s 2.0 peak) are rare normal variants or true anomalies—catalog statistics suggest they occur infrequently but reproducibly.
Exact plateau duration varies slightly (30–45 points); the acceptable range is not tightly bounded by current references.
Baseline drift direction/slope may depend on global segment position; no reference shows strong negative drift, so negative trends in queries require extra scrutiny.
